newsitem.title: USA: EDS stock plunges following poor earnings report, forecast.
newsitem.headline: EDS stock plunges following poor earnings report, forecast.

text.p: Electronic Data Systems Inc. stock lost 14 percent of its value Friday after the computer services company reported declining earnings and forecast a rocky year ahead.
Shares of Dallas-based EDS fell by $6.125 to $36.94 in heavy trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where they were the most active issue with more than 5.2 million shares traded.

EDS, a leading global provider of information services, said Thursday that, excluding special charges, its net income in the second quarter fell to $192.4 million, or 39 cents a share, from $246.6 million, or 51 cents a share, a year earlier, also excluding charges.

The company also said that, due to an expected erosion of anticipated revenues and earnings, principally from a small number of contracts booked before 1996, it anticipates 1997 earnings in the range of $1.90 to $2 a share before any charge -- well below its earlier estimate of $2.30 to $2.35 a share before any charge.
"Our results for the quarter and expectations for the year are not only disappointing but unacceptable," Chairman Les Alberthal said in a statement.
"Clearly, we have work to do, which is one reason we undertook the most intensive examination and redesign of our business in EDS' history earlier this year."
